tools.name: ocp_help
tools.description:
OCP — Help & routing. Call this for any prompt containing 'OCP', 'BimPlus', 'construction platform', or when you are unsure which tool to use.
Trigger phrases: 'what can OCP do', 'help with OCP', 'what tools are available', 'open OCP', 'connect to OCP'.
Returns a summary of available capabilities and example prompts.

tools.name: set_bimplus_config
tools.description:
OCP — Configure. Set connection state: token, base URL, team, credentials.
Use when authentication or API calls fail because config is missing or outdated.
Call once, then run task tools.
Returns masked config snapshot.

tool_catalog_mode.description: Tool exposure mode: smart (default), hybrid, or full

max_auto_tools.description: Max autogenerated tools to expose in hybrid/full mode (0 = no limit)

tool_catalog_fallback_mode.description: When mode=smart, expose fallback catalog from: off, hybrid, or full

tool_catalog_fallback_limit.description: When mode=smart, number of fallback auto tools to expose (0 disables fallback)

usage_webhook_url.description: HTTP collector for usage log events; empty string disables shipping and keeps logs local-only

usage_webhook_mode.description: How often usage logs are shipped: realtime (every event), session_start (once per server start, sending what previous sessions left), daily (once per UTC day), or off

tools.name: get_bimplus_config
tools.description:
OCP — Show config. Read the current OCP connection state.
Use before troubleshooting auth/team/project errors.
Returns masked token field.

tools.name: set_bimplus_sso_token
tools.description:
OCP — SSO login. Paste a browser/SSO Bearer token to authorize.
After logging into the OCP portal, paste the access token here.
Validates via GET /v2/authorize and saves to config.

token.description: SSO access token to use for API authorization

token_type.description: Authorization scheme, for example Bearer or Identity

tools.name: start_sso_login
tools.description:
OCP — SSO browser login. Open the OCP/Allplan login page in the browser and capture the token automatically via OAuth2 PKCE — no manual copy-paste required.
Primary tool for: 'login to OCP with SSO', 'browser login', 'login via portal'.
Opens browser → user logs in → token saved automatically.
Optional: timeout_seconds (default 120).

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the browser login to complete

tools.name: list_team_projects
tools.description:
OCP — List projects. Show all projects in a team, optionally filtered by name or ID.
Primary tool for: 'list all projects', 'show OCP projects', 'search project by name'.
Optional: team_slug (uses config default), query, limit.
Returns normalized rows with id/name/number/status.

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter across project id/name/number

limit.description: Maximum number of matched projects to return

tools.name: list_project_models
tools.description:
OCP — List models. Show available models (divisions) in a project, optionally filtered.
Primary tool for: 'show model names', 'which models are available', 'list OCP models'.
Optional: project_id, team_slug, query, limit.
Returns normalized rows with id/name; flags the currently selected model.

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

project_id.description: Project UUID (uses config default if omitted)

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter across model id/name

limit.description: Maximum number of matched models to return

tools.name: list_my_teams
tools.description:
OCP — List teams. Show all teams available to the current user, optionally filtered.
Primary tool for: 'list my teams', 'show OCP teams', 'which teams do I have access to'.
Optional: query, limit.
Returns normalized rows with id/name/slug.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring filter across team id/name/slug

limit.description: Maximum number of matched teams to return

tools.name: search_objects
tools.description:
OCP — Search objects. Run a filtered object search across a project in one call.
Use for: 'find all Columns with material C30/37', 'search OCP objects by property'.
Required: project_id. Optional: team_slug, discipline_id, filter_name, conditions, filter_string.
Prefer conditions for simple equality filters; filter_string for advanced syntax.
Returns filtered search payload.

conditions.description: Structured filter conditions (Option A). Each item: {attribute_id: string, value: string, attribute_group?: string}. attribute_group defaults to 'tabAttribElement.DivisionID'.

filter_string.description: Raw BimPlus filter string (Option B, advanced). Ignored if conditions is provided.

filter_name.description: Display name for the filter (default: Custom Filter)

team_slug.description: Team slug — uses config default if omitted

tools.name: count_elements_by_type
tools.description:
OCP — Count by type. Count objects per element type in a project, or scoped to one model.
Primary tool for: 'list object types and counts', 'how many elements are in OCP?', 'how many <Type> exist in <model>?'.
Required: project_id. Optional: team_slug, model_id, include_zero, max_concurrency.
The underlying BimPlus elements endpoint has no per-model scoping, so when model_id is given this switches to the topology/filter pipeline (same one search_objects uses) grouped by element type and restricted to that model's layer, instead of the project-wide fetch. Use list_project_models to find a model_id. Falls back to the config default model_id if set.
Returns total objects, totals by discipline (project-wide mode only), and per-type counts.

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

model_id.description: Model/division UUID to scope the count to a single model instead of the whole project (uses config default model_id if omitted and set).

max_concurrency.description: Parallel requests when counting types (project-wide mode only)

tools.name: count_elements_by_property_value
tools.description:
OCP — Count by property. Count elements of one type where a property matches a value.
Primary tool for: 'how many Columns have material C30/37?', 'count OCP elements by property'.
Accepts type name or UUID. Required: project_id, type_name_or_id, property_name, property_value.
Returns matched count, sample IDs, and value distribution.

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

sample_limit.description: How many matching object IDs to include as sample

tools.name: list_pset_property_values
tools.description:
OCP — List Pset property values. Unique values of a property nested inside a Pset for all elements of one type (e.g. Room / Pset_Revit_Other / Category Code).
Use for: 'unique values of Category Code on Rooms', 'what values does <Pset property> take'.
Unlike count_elements_by_property_value (flat/top-level properties only), this resolves the property's internal attribute GUID and uses the same settings/filter -> exportobjects -> selections/{id}/filters/{id} pipeline the BimPlus Explorer UI uses, so it can reach Pset-nested (free attribute) properties.
Required: project_id, type_name_or_id, pset_name, property_name. Optional: team_slug, max_elements.
Returns the resolved attribute id plus a value -> count breakdown.

type_name_or_id.description: Element type name (case-insensitive) or UUID, e.g. 'Room'

pset_name.description: Property set (free attribute group) name, e.g. 'Pset_Revit_Other'

property_name.description: Property name inside the Pset, e.g. 'Category Code'

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

max_elements.description: Cap on how many elements of the type to include in the selection

tools.name: find_elements_by_properties
tools.description:
OCP — Find elements by properties. Multi-condition AND search by plain property name/value pairs — no attribute GUIDs required, and works for both flat/general properties AND Pset-nested (free attribute) properties in the same call.
Use for: 'find Rooms where Level=2 and Category Code=13-15 11 34 11', 'which Stairs have Fire Rating = 60min'.
Each condition is resolved automatically: properties already present on the bulk element fetch are matched client-side (fast); properties not found there are treated as Pset-nested and resolved via the same settings/filter -> exportobjects -> selections/{id}/filters/{id} pipeline list_pset_property_values uses. Optionally hint pset_name per condition to disambiguate a property name that exists in more than one Pset.
Required: project_id, type_name_or_id, conditions (non-empty list of {property_name, value, pset_name?}). Optional: team_slug, case_sensitive, trim_whitespace, max_elements, sample_limit.
Returns matched object ids plus a per-condition breakdown of how each was resolved.

type_name_or_id.description: Element type name (case-insensitive) or UUID, e.g. 'Room'

pset_name.description: Optional Pset (free attribute group) name hint, e.g. 'Pset_Revit_Other', to disambiguate

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

max_elements.description: Cap on how many elements of the type to scan

sample_limit.description: How many matching object ids to include in the result

tools.name: bulk_update_property_by_filter
tools.description:
OCP — Bulk update. Update an attribute for elements selected by a property filter.
Primary tool for safe OCP mass edits; replaces per-object update loops.
Safety flow: first run dry_run=true to preview, then dry_run=false + confirm=true to apply.
Supports safety limits, batching, and optional read-back verification.
Returns matched/updated/failed counts and verification summary.

filter_property_name.description: Property name used to select elements

filter_property_value.description: Property value used to select elements

attribute_id.description: Target attribute UUID for the update endpoint

new_value.description: New value to assign for all matched elements

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

target_property_name.description: Optional property name used for read-back verification

dry_run.description: If true, only preview affected IDs without writing

confirm.description: Must be true to execute writes when dry_run=false

batch_size.description: Number of object IDs per update request

verify.description: Run read-back verification after successful writes

sample_limit.description: How many IDs to include in preview output

tools.name: create_issue
tools.description:
OCP — Create issue. Create a new BimPlus issue/BCF topic, optionally pinned to every element of a given type (or an explicit list of element IDs).
Primary tool for: 'create an issue for all Stairs titled X', 'raise an OCP issue on these elements'.
There is no auto-generated tool for this — BimPlus's create-issue endpoint is a POST, and this server's default catalog mode only surfaces GET endpoints automatically; this hand-crafted tool is the supported path for issue creation regardless of tool_catalog_mode.
Safety flow: first run dry_run=true to preview which elements would be pinned, then dry_run=false + confirm=true to actually create the issue and attach pins.
Required: project_id, title. Optional: team_slug, description, status, priority, type_name_or_id, object_ids, max_pins.
Returns the created issue id plus pin attach/fail counts.

status.description: Issue status string (optional, BimPlus default applies if omitted)

type_name_or_id.description: Element type name (case-insensitive) or UUID; every matching element is pinned to the issue

object_ids.description: Explicit element UUIDs to pin, in addition to/instead of type_name_or_id

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

max_pins.description: Safety limit on how many elements can be pinned in one call

dry_run.description: If true, only preview the issue and pin candidates without creating anything

confirm.description: Must be true to actually create the issue when dry_run=false

sample_limit.description: How many element IDs to include in preview/result output

tools.name: update_issue
tools.description:
OCP — Update issue. Change an existing BimPlus issue's title/description/status/priority and/or pin more elements to it (by type or explicit IDs). Never removes existing pins.
Primary tool for: 'mark issue X as resolved', 'add these elements to issue X', 'update the priority on issue X'.
Fetches the current issue first and only overwrites the fields you provide, so omitted fields are preserved rather than wiped (the underlying BimPlus endpoint is a full update).
Safety flow: first run dry_run=true to preview the change and any new pin candidates, then dry_run=false + confirm=true to apply.
Required: project_id, issue_id. Optional: team_slug, title, description, status, priority, type_name_or_id, object_ids, max_pins.
Returns the applied changes plus pin attach/fail counts.

issue_id.description: UUID of the issue to update

title.description: New issue title (BimPlus 'name' field); omit to leave unchanged

description.description: New description; omit to leave unchanged

status.description: New status string; omit to leave unchanged

priority.description: New priority string; omit to leave unchanged

type_name_or_id.description: Element type name (case-insensitive) or UUID; every matching element is additionally pinned to the issue

object_ids.description: Explicit element UUIDs to additionally pin

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

max_pins.description: Safety limit on how many new elements can be pinned in one call

dry_run.description: If true, only preview the change and pin candidates without applying anything

confirm.description: Must be true to actually apply the update when dry_run=false

sample_limit.description: How many element IDs to include in preview/result output

tools.name: project_dashboard_insights
tools.description:
OCP — Project dashboard. Build a full project summary in one call.
Primary tool for: 'show OCP project dashboard', 'project summary', 'top element types and issue stats'.
Required: project_id. Optional: team_slug, top_n_types, sample_issue_limit, include_element_samples, area_property_names, volume_property_names.
Returns normalized dashboard JSON ready for UI/reporting.

team_slug.description: Team slug (uses config default if omitted)

top_n_types.description: How many top element types to include by count

sample_issue_limit.description: How many issues to include as sample rows

include_element_samples.description: Include sample element IDs for top types (extra API calls)

area_property_names.description: Property names treated as area candidates (default includes area/netarea/grossarea)

volume_property_names.description: Property names treated as volume candidates (default includes volume/netvolume/grossvolume)

tools.name: mark_chat_start
tools.description:
OCP — Mark chat start (analytics). Call this ONCE, as the first OCP action in a new conversation, before any other OCP/BimPlus tool.
Purpose: records only that a new chat began — no message text, no user data. Skip it if you have already called it earlier in this same conversation.
Returns a short acknowledgement.

tools.name: log_note
tools.description:
OCP — Log note (analytics). Record a short, labelled free-text note to the usage log. Generic: use it whenever a skill or instruction tells you to, with the 'kind' label and text that instruction specifies.
Do NOT include secrets, credentials, tokens, or personal data. Keep text under ~500 characters. Returns a short acknowledgement.

kind.description: A short label categorizing the note (e.g. as directed by a skill). Defaults to 'note' if omitted.

text.description: A short note. No secrets or personal data.

tools.description: Gets the issue rights for a specific issue. (GET /v2/{teamSlug}/issues/{issueId}/rights). Prefer smart tools first.

tools.name: get_by_teamslug_projects_by_projectid_attachments
tools.description: Gets all attachments for a team, project, object, or issue. (GET /v2/{teamSlug}/projects/{projectId}/attachments). Prefer smart tools first.

recycleBin.description:
Optional. This query parameter indicates whether to include attachments from the recycle bin. 

 Example: `?recycleBin=true`

versionsShortInfo.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies whether to include short information about attachment versions. 

 Example: `?versionsShortInfo=true`

revision.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies a particular revision of the attachment to retrieve. 

 Example: `?revision=3`

projectOnly.description:
Optional. This query parameter indicates whether to filter attachments to only those related to the project. 

 Example: `?projectOnly=true`

attachmenttype.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies the types of attachments to filter by. 

 The values should be valid `AttachmentType` enums converted to Guid. 

 Example: `?attachmenttype=type1&type2`

page.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies the page number. It must be used together with 'pageSize' query parameter, otherwise it is ignored. 

 Example : `?page=1&pageSize=5`

pageSize.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies the page size. It must be used together with 'page' query parameter, otherwise it is ignored. 

 Example : `?pageSize=5&page=1`

sortColumn.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies the column by which the results should be sorted. If it is not followed by 'sortDirection' query parameter then 'ascending' sort is used by default. 

 Example : `?sortColumn=colname`

sortDirection.description:
Optional. This query parameter specifies the direction of sorting. It can be either `asc` (ascending) or `desc` (descending). It must be used together with 'sortColumn' query parameter, otherwise it is ignored. 

 Example : `?sortColumn=colname&sortDirection=desc`

filter.description: Optional. This query parameter is used to retrieve a specific filter value from the query string of an HTTP request. This parameter is typically used to filter data based on certain criteria provided by the client.

filter.description:
Original parameter name: $filter. Optional. This query parameter specifies the filter criteria for the data. 

 Example: `$filter=Name eq 'Project1' and Status ne 'Completed'`. 

 The method replaces certain keywords (eq, lt, gt, ne, le, ge) with their corresponding symbols (=, <, >, <>, <=, >=) and splits the filter string into parts using and and or as delimiters.

orderby.description:
Original parameter name: $orderby. Optional. This query parameter specifies the sorting order of the data. 

 Example: `$orderby=Name asc`. 

 The method reads this parameter directly and assigns it to the Sort property of the QueryParameters object.

skip.description:
Original parameter name: $skip. Optional. This query parameter specifies the number of records to skip. 

 Example: `$skip=10`. 

 The method attempts to parse this parameter as an integer and assigns it to the Offset property of the QueryParameters object.

top.description:
Original parameter name: $top. Optional. This query parameter specifies the number of records to return. 

 Example: `$top=5`. 

 The method attempts to parse this parameter as an integer and assigns it to the PageSize property of the QueryParameters object.
